text: # Incident Report: Duplicate Billing Cycle Run for Postpaid Segment **Document ID:** INC_C04_INC_2026_0163 **Category:** C04 — Billing & Invoices **Department:** Billing **Customer Scope:** all **Last Updated:** 2026-07-08 **Version:** 1.0 **Source Authority:** Internal Knowledge Base --- ## Summary A scheduling error in the billing batch job caused ~12,000 postpaid customers to be billed twice for the June cycle. ## Detection Method Identified during routine NOC dashboard review, ahead of any customer-reported tickets. ## Timeline Detected via automated reconciliation checks; batch job halted within 40 minutes; duplicate charges auto-reversed within 48 hours; affected customers notified via SMS. | Time | Event | Observation | Action | |---|---|---|---| | T+0 | Fault detected | Alarm/ticket volume triggers investigation | On-call engineer paged | | T+10m | Initial triage | Affected scope estimated | Field/remote team engaged as needed | | T+Xh | Interim mitigation | Partial service restored where possible | Status page updated | | T+Yh | Full restoration | Service confirmed normal | Incident closed, RCA initiated if required | ## Customer Impact Estimated customers affected and service categories impacted are recorded in the internal incident-management system (ref: INC-2026-0163). Customer-facing status was published under Network > Service Status for the outage duration. ## Initial Hypothesis The initial working theory pointed to the most probable cause based on alarm signatures and affected-scope pattern; this was confirmed or revised during investigation. ## Investigation The response team correlated alarm data, affected-site/customer patterns, and any recent change or third-party activity in the area to isolate
title: Duplicate Billing Cycle Run for Postpaid Segment
